title: Image rotation, signature policy, and preflight smokecheck notes
content:
Purpose
This note captures a pragmatic operational pattern for private deployments: rotating container images and signing keys, enforcing signature policy in GitOps pipelines (ArgoCD), running preflight smokechecks, and implementing safe rollback triggers. It is intended for SREs, platform engineers, and release owners who run Dedicated/Private installs (VPC or on-prem).

Context and constraints
- Many customers run in airgapped or restricted VPCs with limited egress; pushing images requires an upstream promotion step and local registry sync.
- We must maintain reproducible artifacts: signed images + attestations + SBOM.
- Terraform modules declare registry endpoints, imagePullSecrets, and optional attestations metadata. Keep TF changes minimal during rotation windows.
- Goal: Minimize blast radius when rotating images or signing keys and avoid frequent operator restarts.

High-level flow (image rotation + release promotion)
1) Build + tag artifacts in CI (hosted builder or isolated builder VM). Produce: image:sha256, SBOM (cyclonedx), cosign signature, attestation (in-toto or custom).
2) Store artifacts in central artifact bucket + registry (internal). Record artifact metadata in a release manifest (yaml).
3) Promote: sync artifacts to customer registry (airgapped proxy sync or direct push). Use signed manifests and verify on target.
4) Update GitOps repo (app-of-apps pattern) with new image digests and attestations references; open PR.
5) Preflight: pipeline triggers smokecheck jobs against a staging namespace that mirrors customer cluster (lightweight).
6) Merge: ArgoCD picks up change and deploys. Monitor rollout, run canary checks.
7) Post-rollout: rotate keys only after successful deployments and a retention window.

Key mechanics and automation notes
- Image digests only: always pin image by digest in Helm values and Kustomize resources (no floating tags). Example Helm values snippet: image:
  repository: private.registry.example.com/redwood/runtime
  digest: sha256:abcd...
  pullPolicy: IfNotPresent

- Cosign + Sigstore: use cosign to sign images and generate attestation bundles. Store the cosign public key in the customer KMS or in the cluster as a Kubernetes secret with strict RBAC. For airgapped installs, cosign key pairs should be generated on customer side and the public key uploaded to our signing-verification service.

- Signature policy enforcement in ArgoCD: add a lightweight admission-like gate in the repo pipeline (pre-commit CI job) and a runtime verification plugin in ArgoCD. We recommend the "argocd-image-validators" pattern: run `cosign verify` against the image digest referenced in the PR. If verification fails, the PR check should block merge.

- Terraform modules: variable patterns & idempotency
  - registry_host (string), image_pull_secret_name (string, optional), enable_attestation (bool), allowed_signers (list of strings).
  - Keep module changes additive. If rotation requires new secrets, create a new secret resource with timestamped name and update pods via a rolling restart controller to consume the new secret. Avoid in-place replacement of Secret by default (use new Secret + annotation on deployment for controlled rollout).
  - Example practices: use `random_pet` suffix for non-sensitive resource names in test/preview stacks, but avoid for customer prod stacks. Document mappings in module README.

- Helm hooks and upgrade strategy
  - Use Helm post-install/post-upgrade hooks for lightweight schema migrations and for triggering smokechecks (not for heavy operations).
  - Prefer Kubernetes-native rolling updates over Helm hooks for workload restarts. Use `maxUnavailable` set conservatively (10-20%).
  - For CRD changes: follow two-release CRD strategy: ship new CRD with a new version as non-breaking first, migrate controllers, then switch default in a subsequent release. Maintain CRD conversion webhooks when necessary.

Preflight smokecheck pattern (fast, repeatable)
- Objective: catch obvious runtime regressions before promoting to customer clusters. Time budget: ~10-15 minutes. Steps:
  1) Deploy new image to an ephemeral namespace in a dedicated staging cluster (k8s cluster that mirrors runtime config).
  2) Run health probes: readiness/liveness, sample inference with small prompt, KV-cache warmup (if applicable), common API surface smoke (tokenization, streaming handshake).
  3) Validate telemetry: ensure request traces, token counts, and latency fall within N% of baseline.
  4) Run signature verification to confirm attestation attachment.
  5) Generate a smokecheck report (JSON + simple HTML) and attach to the PR for operator review.

Automated rollback criteria and signals
- Automatic rollback should be conservative. Trigger rollback when two or more of the following hold within a 10-minute window post-rollout:
  - error rate increases by > 3x baseline and absolute error rate > 1%
  - median tail latency (p95) increases by > 2x baseline and > 500ms absolute
  - key metric (e.g., model stderr or generation token errors) shows frequent NaN/empty outputs
  - attestation verification failures detected for deployed pods
- Rollback mechanism: ArgoCD rollback to previous commit (app-of-apps) + run post-rollback smokecheck. Escalate to on-call if rollback fails.

Image signature key rotation (recommended safe path)
1) Generate new cosign key pair in secure environment (customer KMS or HSM if available).
2) Publish new public key to verification endpoints and to ArgoCD verification config. Keep old key active for a transition window (30-90 days depending on risk tolerance).
3) Re-sign artifacts with new key as part of an incremental rebuild/promotion cycle. Avoid mass re-signing every existing image unless necessary.
4) When old key is retired, make sure SBOM and attestations remain addressable via stored artifacts.

Airgap and OCI proxy considerations
- For airgapped customers, we operate a "push proxy" flow: push signed images to a controlled artifact bucket, customer runs an approved sync process to pull images into their registry. Document required fields in the manifest (digest, cosign signature URL, SBOM URL, attestation blob).
- Use `skopeo copy --dest-creds` and `regsync` patterns in documented scripts for registry sync. Example script lines (simplified):
  skopeo copy docker://public.registry/repo@sha256:... docker://private.registry/repo@sha256:... --dest-creds user:pass

Checklist for a rotation window (preflight to post)
- Pre-window: update release manifest, verify signatures, run smokecheck in staging, notify customers (if required), open JIRA ticket with impact SLA
- During window: follow app-of-apps PR flow, monitor ArgoCD sync events, check smokecheck attach, watch SLO dashboards and Pod events
- Post-window: confirm canary window success (24-72 hrs), rotate verification keys if required, archive old artifacts to read-only storage, update Terraform module vars to remove temporary flags

Troubleshooting playbook (quick actions)
- If ArgoCD fails to sync due to signature mismatch: run `cosign verify --key <pub.key> <image>` locally against a copy of the image digest; confirm which pub key ArgoCD config references.
- If imagePullBackOff in customer cluster: validate imagePullSecret, registry reachable (DNS, firewall), and that digest exists in target registry. Use `crane manifest` or `skopeo inspect` to confirm digest presence.
- If rollout stalls due to CRD conversion: rollback to previous release and open a CRD migration task; avoid manual CRD edits in customer clusters unless guided.

Open questions (needs follow-up)
- How do we standardize attestation storage location for airgapped customers so that verification can be performed offline? (proposal: embed attestation as OCI artifact alongside image manifest).
- Default transition window for cosign key rotation (suggest 60 days) — agree on customer-facing SLAs.
- Should Terraform modules provide a "secret rotation controller" CR that handles lifecycle of imagePullSecrets? Explore prototype.

Action items
- (Evan) Draft a small RFC describing attestation embedding in OCI manifests, include timeline and backward compatibility notes. (Due 2025-03-20)
- (Maya) Prototype an ArgoCD pre-sync plugin that runs `cosign verify` against PR-referenced digests and posts results to the PR status. (Due 2025-03-10)
- (Luis) Add `allowed_signers` and `attestation_url` variables to the private-deploy Terraform module and write tests for idempotent updates. (Due 2025-03-17)

References and helpful commands
- cosign basics: https://github.com/sigstore/cosign
- skopeo example sync: https://github.com/containers/skopeo
- example ArgoCD image validator: github.com/redwood-inference/argocd-validators (internal)
- Helpful commands:
    cosign verify --key ./pub.key private.registry.example.com/repo@sha256:abcd...
    skopeo inspect docker://private.registry.example.com/repo@sha256:abcd...
    crane manifest private.registry.example.com/repo@sha256:abcd...

Notes: keep this doc intentionally operational and terse. It should live alongside the other private deploy playbooks but focus on the intersection of image signing, rotation policy, terraform-safe module changes, and a lightweight smokecheck pattern for safe promotion.
